title: A Contact for the Extraction
premise: August Galloway has spent six years translating for peace delegations in the contested border city of Vessengrad, hiding the fact that he once worked for the intelligence service he now claims to despise. When his handler, Marta, turns up dead and a calendar invite from her account summons him to a dead drop, August realizes someone is using his buried past to force him to smuggle a defector's testimony across the border before the checkpoint rotations bury it forever. Hunted by the service he betrayed, the militia that killed Marta, and the delegation colleagues he's lied to for years, August assembles an unlikely crew of translators, drivers, and a teenage courier who become the family he never had. He trades his secret—the location of a massacre archive worth killing for—in exchange for safe passage, and the book ends with the testimony going public, August choosing exile with his found family rather than a return to invisibility.
about_author: Casper Eriksen is the pen name of a former NGO field worker who spent a decade in border regions where translation was often the only thing standing between negotiation and violence. They write thrillers about the invisible people—interpreters, drivers, couriers—who keep fragile peace processes alive.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag by the Door
chapters.summary: POV: August. August interprets the opening session of the Halvern Peace Delegation in Vessengrad, smoothing over a hostile exchange while mentally rehearsing his cover story. At his apartment, we see the packed go-bag and the false identity documents taped beneath a drawer. Emotional beat: controlled loneliness—the discipline of a man who has made himself unmemorable on purpose.

chapters.title: Marta's Last Correction
chapters.summary: POV: August. Marta, his handler and the only person who knows what he was, critiques his translation choices over cheap wine and warns him the delegation is a performance for cameras. She mentions 'the archive' once and stops herself. August walks home through checkpoint queues, noting the rotation schedule out of habit. Emotional beat: warmth threaded with dread.

chapters.title: Invitation from a Dead Woman
chapters.summary: POV: August. Marta is found floating in the Kessel Canal, officially a drowning. That night August's phone buzzes: a calendar invite from her account, tomorrow, 06:00, the old tram depot. He knows dead handlers don't send invitations. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out—the moment invisibility fails.

chapters.title: Six A.M. at the Tram Depot
chapters.summary: POV: August. August goes armed with nothing but nerve. Instead of a trap he finds Yara, a sixteen-year-old courier Marta mentored, carrying a sealed drive and a note in Marta's handwriting naming August as 'the extractor.' Militia scouts sweep the depot; the two barely escape together. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance born under fire.

chapters.title: What the Drive Says
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Through Yara's eyes, we learn the drive holds a defector's recorded testimony about the Ostrov massacre and the archive's location—evidence implicating both militia commanders and delegation 'observers.' Yara trusts August because Marta did, and resents needing him. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: The Delegation's Bright Lie
chapters.summary: POV: August. Back at the delegation, August translates a communiqué he knows is false while scanning colleagues for the leak that got Marta killed. Deputy head Ilse Rook watches him a beat too long. Emotional beat: paranoia in a room full of handshakes—everyone smiling, someone lying.

chapters.title: The Man Who Knew His Old Name
chapters.summary: POV: August. A 'security consultant' named Drevin corners August at the hotel bar and uses his real surname from his intelligence years. He offers protection in exchange for the drive. August refuses and immediately starts planning his own disappearance. Emotional beat: the past arriving with a polite smile and a threat.

chapters.title: Safehouse of Strangers
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Yara brings August to Marta's hidden network: Tomas, a disgraced checkpoint guard; Lien, a deaf sign-language interpreter who reads rooms better than anyone; and the widow Oksana, who feeds everyone. August, the professional loner, is fed, questioned, and claimed. Emotional beat: the terrifying warmth of being known.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV: Tomas. Tomas maps the border rotations: in four days, the Northgate checkpoint shifts to a militia-controlled unit that will hold the city in lockdown. The testimony must cross before then. They draft three extraction plans, each with a different fatal flaw. Emotional beat: hope as a math problem with a deadline.

chapters.title: Ilse Rook's Quiet Offer
chapters.summary: POV: August. Ilse privately reveals she knows about the drive—and that she isn't Drevin's. She's a whistleblower inside the delegation who needs the testimony as badly as they do, and offers delegation vehicles as cover. August must decide whether to trust another handler. Emotional beat: the ache of learning to extend trust twice.

chapters.title: The Archive's Coordinates
chapters.summary: POV: August. The drive's final file is encrypted; opening it requires a passphrase only August would know—a phrase from his intelligence days, proving Marta built this plan around him years ago. He decrypts the archive location and realizes she chose him not despite his past but because of it. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into being chosen.

chapters.title: Drevin Closes the Net
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. Drevin's men raid the safehouse network, seizing Oksana's café and putting the city on alert. Yara, out on a supply run, evades capture and must decide whether to lead the militia to the others or warn them and lose the drive window. Emotional beat: a teenager making adult choices with a racing heart.

chapters.title: Burning the Safehouse
chapters.summary: POV: Tomas. The network scatters, torching documents and splitting the drive's copies. Tomas is captured covering the others' escape and refuses to talk under interrogation, buying hours with lies. Emotional beat: sacrifice without applause—the quiet heroism of the invisible.

chapters.title: The Price on the Table
chapters.summary: POV: August. Drevin contacts August directly: Tomas's life for the archive coordinates. August, knowing the coordinates are the one secret worth killing for, prepares to trade them—and secretly plans to trade false ones. Emotional beat: the cold clarity of a man deciding exactly how far he'll go.

chapters.title: Lien Reads the Room
chapters.summary: POV: Lien. Lien, observing the exchange site from across the plaza, spots the second militia team Drevin never intended to call off—a double-cross inside the double-cross. Her silent warning via Yara's phone saves the handoff. Emotional beat: the network's least visible member becomes its eyes.

chapters.title: False Coordinates, True Fire
chapters.summary: POV: August. August hands over forged coordinates; the militia raids an empty grain silo and realizes they've been played, putting a citywide kill order on August. Tomas is released into chaos and escapes in the confusion. Emotional beat: triumph with a timer attached.

chapters.title: Northgate, Last Shift
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. With hours before the checkpoint rotation, the crew runs the real plan: testimony hidden in Ilse's delegation vehicle, August riding with Yara in a produce truck as backup. At the gate, a guard recognizes August's face from the kill order. Emotional beat: everything narrowing to one barrier arm and thirty seconds.

chapters.title: Thirty Seconds at the Barrier
chapters.summary: POV: August. The recognizing guard is a man August once translated for—a man he once saved from a false charge. In a whispered exchange, August asks for the debt back. The barrier lifts. Ilse's vehicle crosses with the testimony; August and Yara are waved through behind it. Emotional beat: a single act of grace repaying years of small decencies.

chapters.title: What Drevin Deserves
chapters.summary: POV: August. Across the border, August faces a choice: disappear, or ensure Drevin falls. He trades the true archive location not to Drevin but to Ilse's international contacts, along with evidence of Drevin's role in Marta's death—justice outside any court that would hear it. Emotional beat: refusing revenge, choosing reckoning.

chapters.title: The Testimony Goes Public
chapters.summary: POV: Yara. The defector's recording airs across three networks; the Ostrov massacre becomes undeniable, delegations collapse in disgrace, and Drevin is arrested at an airport lounge he thought was an exit. Yara watches the footage and finally lets herself cry for Marta. Emotional beat: catharsis—the dead woman's plan completing itself.

chapters.title: The Family at the Kitchen Table
chapters.summary: POV: August. In a rented house across the border, the network regathers: Tomas recovering, Lien teaching Yara to sign, Oksana cooking in a new kitchen. August unpacks the go-bag for the first time in six years and puts the false documents in the fire. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not performed.

chapters.title: A Contact for the Extraction
chapters.summary: POV: August. Months later, a new invitation arrives—from Ilse, about another delegation, another border, another truth that needs carrying. August looks at the go-bag he no longer keeps packed, then at the people around the table, and says yes—but this time, they all go together. Emotional beat: the loner's arc complete; extraction now means bringing everyone home.
